newsitem.title: USA: Ukrainian diplomat charged with drunken driving.
newsitem.headline: Ukrainian diplomat charged with drunken driving.

text.p: A Ukrainian embassy official is claiming diplomatic immunity after allegedly causing a three-car accident in northwest Washington, a police spokesman said on Sunday.
It was the fourth alleged drunken driving case this year involving diplomats from the former Soviet Union.

Olesy Yarotskiy, 45, was charged with driving while intoxicated, tailgating, failing to pay attention and failing to produce a driver's permit after her 1986 Chrysler LeBaron struck a second car late on Saturday, pushing it into the car ahead of it.
No one was injured in the accident.
Sgt. Joseph Gentile said Yarotskiy was claiming diplomatic immunity in the case.

The State Department said on Friday it expected to ask Kyrgyzstan to waive the immunity of Erkinbek Atabekov, a second secretary at the Kyrgyz embassy, who failed a Breathalyzer test after his van was involved in a collision with two parked vehicles in a Washington street on Thursday.
No comment was immediately available from the State Department on whether it would also ask Ukraine to waive the immunity of Yarotskiy.

The most serious case this year was that of Georgian diplomat Gueorgui Makharadze, whose immunity was waived by his government after he was involved in a car crash that killed a teenage girl in Washington in January.
Makharadze pleaded innocent to charges of involuntary manslaughter and aggravated assault and was scheduled to be tried starting July 21.
